definitions.explanation: The padded glove-and-forearm protector worn in {剣道|けんどう} (kendo). Also refers to similar wrist-and-forearm guards worn with traditional armor or in other martial arts.
In kendo, a scoring strike to the opponent's wrist/forearm. Called out as 'kote!' when delivered.

examples.japanese: {小手|こて}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧。
examples.english: To put on the kendo gauntlets.

examples.japanese: ⟦{練習|れんしゅう}→練習：05323_renshuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧、{小手|こて}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{丁寧|ていねい}→丁寧：00896_teinei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{干|ほ}した→干す：00115_hosu⟧。
examples.english: After practice, I carefully aired out my kote.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}く→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧{小手|こて}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧もの⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{買|か}い{替|か}えた→買い替える：19456_kaikaeru⟧。
examples.english: I replaced my worn-out kote with new ones.

examples.japanese: ⟦{鋭|するど}い→鋭い：02347_surudoi⟧{小手|こて}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{決|き}めた→決める：00858_kimeru⟧。
examples.english: He landed a sharp strike to the wrist.

examples.japanese: ⟦{試合|しあい}→試合：01601_shiai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{小手|こて}⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{勝負|しょうぶ}→勝負：01437_shoubu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ついた。
examples.english: The match was decided by a single kote strike.

examples.japanese: ⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{動|うご}き→動き：11926_ugoki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}んで→読む：00426_yomu⟧、すばやく{小手|こて}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}った→打つ：01221_utsu⟧。
examples.english: Reading my opponent's movement, I quickly struck their kote.

notes:
Two related meanings centered on the wrist/forearm: the protective armor itself, and the strike that targets it.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小手|こて}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧: to strike the kote
- {小手|こて}⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧: a single kote point
- {小手面|こてめん}: a kote-followed-by-men combination strike

KENDO CONTEXT:
There are four scoring targets in kendo: ⟦{面|めん}→面：09933_men⟧ (head), {小手|こて} (wrist), {胴|どう} (torso), and {突|つ}き (throat thrust). When a strike lands, the striker shouts the name of the target. The wrist gauntlets themselves are also worn during ⟦{剣道|けんどう}→剣道：04452_kendou⟧, {薙刀|なぎなた}, and some armored martial arts.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {籠手|こて}: same meaning but with the older/traditional kanji writing — common in historical armor contexts
- {手甲|てっこう}: hand-back covering worn by laborers and travelers — covers the back of the hand and forearm
